title: FireAxe: Partitioned FPGA-Accelerated Simulation of Large-Scale RTL Designs
problem: Existing FPGA-based RTL simulation platforms cannot handle custom hardware designs whose resource requirements exceed a single FPGA's capacity. This limits pre-silicon validation of large-scale and complex hardware systems.
motivation: Pre-silicon validation and end-to-end system evaluation are critical for hardware development as they reveal complex interactions between hardware components, system software, and applications.
method: FireAxe automatically divides a hardware design across multiple FPGA chips (reconfigurable hardware) using a compiler called FireRipper, with engineer guidance and feedback on how the pieces connect and simulation speed. It offers an accurate mode that preserves exact timing throughout the design, and a fast mode that runs quicker by reducing accuracy only where the FPGA pieces connect. Simulations run at 1.6 million cycles per second on local FPGAs and 1 million cycles per second on AWS F1 FPGAs, enabling flexible scaling from local to cloud resources.
key_novelty: Automatically dividing hardware designs across multiple FPGA chips while maintaining exact cycle-by-cycle timing and enabling flexible scaling from local to cloud resources.
contributions: FireRipper compiler enabling push-button user-guided RTL partitioning across multiple FPGAs
Dual simulation modes balancing fidelity (exact-mode) versus performance (fast-mode at partition boundaries)
First cycle-exact simulation of unprecedented scale including largest OoO cores and 24-core SoCs
Discovery of subtle RTL bugs through full-stack simulation in <2 hours versus weeks in commercial simulators

metrics.other: RTL bug discovery in <2 hours vs weeks in commercial simulator

limitations: Fast-mode sacrifices fidelity at partition boundaries; detailed trade-offs between different partition strategies not discussed.
